extracted.intended_audience: reporters and journalism students covering investigations, hearings, and public meetings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reporting on investigations, legislative hearings, and public meetings: how to choose what matters, present testimony, and write vivid, concise accounts that emphasize significance over trivia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simple, clear explanation of significant parts
rubrics_metrics.description: Simple, clear explanation of the meaning of significant parts of the proceedings
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page emphasizes plain-language explanation so readers understand why parts of the proceedings matter. Explain the import of key actions and rulings rather than merely listing events. Keep exposition straightforward and avoid unnecessary jargon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lively accounts of debate and vivid description
rubrics_metrics.description: Lively accounts of debate on various measures, and vivid description of persons and scenes connected with them — all add to the interest of the stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bring hearings and meetings to life by summarizing the give-and-take of debate and by using sensory, humanizing details about speakers, witnesses, and the setting. Use scenes and portraiture to increase reader engagement while remaining accurate and fair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overemphasizing insignificant incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: Too often, however, insignificant incidents of casual interest are played up as features of meetings of importance to the subordination or even to the exclusion of matters of vital concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let colorful but trivial occurrences displace coverage of substantive issues. Treat anecdotes and side incidents as supplemental, not as the main focus, unless they materially illuminate the central issue. This is an anti-pattern to avoid when choosing what to highlight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle testimony like a court story
rubrics_metrics.description: Testimony in investigations and hearings sometimes has dramatic phases like that in court trials. The questions and the answers in these proceedings are handled like those in court stories, and testimony is dealt with in much the same manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting testimony, structure coverage to reflect the drama and evidentiary function of exchanges: report key Q&A, establish who is asking and answering, and preserve the narrative rhythm of conflict and clarification. Use the same techniques reporters use in court reporting to capture pivotal testimony and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select vital matters and present them concisely; condense routine details
rubrics_metrics.description: To select the vital matters, to present them concisely, and to condense routine but necessary details into the smallest possible compass in stories of this class, require effort and skill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize core facts and findings; summarize procedural or routine information tersely. Lengthy background or procedural minutiae should be reduced to the minimum needed for reader comprehension. Achieving this economy requires judgment and careful editing.
